definitions.explanation: The tendency to become angry or frustrated quickly. As an adjective, describes a person who is easily irritated.

examples.english: A short temper leads to loss. (Proverb: Haste makes waste.)

examples.japanese: {父|ちち}は{短気|たんき}で、すぐに{怒|おこ}る。
examples.english: My father is short-tempered and gets angry right away.

examples.japanese: {短気|たんき}を{起|お}こさないで、もう{少|すこ}し{待|ま}ってください。
examples.english: Don't lose your temper — please wait a little longer.

notes:
FORMS:
- Predicative: {短気|たんき}だ
- Modifier: {短気|たんき}な + noun
- As noun: {短気|たんき}を{起|お}こす (to lose one's temper)

PROVERB:
{短気|たんき}は{損気|そんき} is a well-known saying meaning that impatience leads to disadvantage. {損気|そんき} is a made-up word created to rhyme with {短気|たんき}.

SIMILAR WORDS:
{気|き}が{短|みじか}い has the same meaning but is a phrase rather than a single word. {怒|おこ}りっぽい means "easily angered" and focuses more on the emotional reaction.
